name: Rejumate

lead: Rejumate is an automatic injection device, made for use with the Rejuran polynucleotide (PN) skin booster from PharmaResearch. A clinician uses it to deliver many tiny injections across the face in one pass.
The aim is skin rejuvenation: texture, hydration and a fresher look. The device automates depth and spacing, which would otherwise depend on hand technique.

paras: Treatment takes place in a clinic. The practitioner fits a multi-needle head, such as a 9-pin 0.8 mm head, and works across facial regions. A published study used 317 injection points to deliver 2 mL of polynucleotide per patient.

Injections into skin can cause temporary redness, swelling, bruising and other injection-site reactions; a qualified practitioner decides suitability. Eyelid skin is thinnest, which the study measured at about 0.53 mm.

studies.title: Analysis of Dermal Thickness Across 10 Areas and Injection Depth After Polynucleotide Injection Using Rejumate Automatic 0.8-mm 9-pin Injector on the Face Using 33-MHz Sonography.
studies.source: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open

chain: Automatic multi-needle injector places PN at shallow depth
Skin booster treatment for smoother, fresher skin
angle.text: It is the delivery tool for polynucleotide skin boosters. Its role is consistency of depth and spacing rather than the active ingredient itself.

lead: Rejumate is an automatic multi-needle injector made by PharmaResearch for delivering polynucleotide (PN) skin boosters such as Rejuran into the skin of the face.[1] Polynucleotide derived from fish is used in aesthetic medicine as a dermal filler, according to Wikipedia.[2]

People seek the treatment to improve skin quality. The device automates the injection pattern and depth so each micro-injection lands in a consistent layer rather than depending on the practitioner's hand speed.[1]

A 2025 study in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Global Open measured facial dermal thickness with 33-MHz ultrasound in 31 patients (average age 48.2) and then evaluated injection depth with the Rejumate 0.8 mm 9-pin injector, finding a consistent average depth of 0.55 mm.[1]

paras: Rejumate fires multiple fine needles at once to place small amounts of PN product into the superficial skin. Automated injectors are described in the literature as increasingly important tools in aesthetic medicine because they aim to give precision and consistency in PN treatments for skin rejuvenation.[1]

A 2025 study of 31 patients (4 men, 27 women, average age 48.2) used ultrasound to measure dermal thickness in 10 to 11 facial areas. Average thickness ranged from 0.53 mm at the lower eyelid to 1.18 mm at the temple and posterior cheek.[1]

Each patient then received a standardised 2 mL PN injection at 317 points with a 0.8 mm needle. Average injection depth was 0.55 mm (standard deviation 0.13 mm), with a median of 0.54 mm and a range of 0.29 to 0.99 mm; the authors reported a high degree of consistency.[1] The study measured injection depth and distribution, not cosmetic outcomes.
No adverse-event data are given in the study summary used here. Thin areas such as the lower eyelid (about 0.53 mm) are noted as relevant to depth selection.[1]
